title: THE CROWD IS PART OF THE PRIVACY
subtitle: WHY SHIELDED USAGE MATTERS.

blocks.text: PRIVACY IS NOT ONLY ABOUT HIDING YOUR TRANSACTION. IT IS ALSO ABOUT WHAT AN OBSERVER CANNOT DISTINGUISH IT FROM.
START WITH THE CROWD.

A shielded pool contains cryptographic notes rather than a public list of ordinary address-to-address payments. When notes are created, commitments are added to a commitment tree. When a note is spent, a nullifier prevents double spending without publicly identifying the commitment that was consumed.

That separation is the beginning of the anonymity-set idea. The public chain can verify that a valid note is being spent without receiving a direct public pointer from that spend to one specific earlier note.
THE OBSERVER SEES VALIDITY. THE LINK IS WHAT GOES MISSING.
WHAT AN ANONYMITY SET REALLY MEANS

An anonymity set is not a magic number that guarantees privacy. It describes the set of possibilities among which a private action may be hidden. In a shielded system, a larger and more active set can make simple linkage less informative, but real privacy also depends on transaction structure, wallet behavior, timing and what happens at pool boundaries.

That distinction matters. Saying that more shielded activity can improve the environment for privacy is reasonable. Saying that every user automatically receives identical privacy merely because a pool contains many notes would be too strong.
ORCHARD CHANGED THE SHAPE

ZIP 224 describes Orchard as a separate anonymity set from earlier Sprout and Sapling pools. Orchard Actions were designed with arity-hiding properties so the number of logical spends and outputs is less directly exposed than in earlier constructions. The design was intended to let Orchard's anonymity set grow efficiently as shielded activity moved into the pool.
POOLS ARE NOT ONE GIANT CLOUD

Different shielded pools have distinct commitment trees and therefore distinct anonymity sets. In 2026, Zcash introduced the Ironwood pool as a successor using the Orchard cryptographic design but with its own commitment tree and chain value pool. Moving between pools is not the same as making an ordinary payment inside one pool.

ZIP 318 states the important privacy consequence directly: within a pool, balances and transaction relationships remain private, while a pool-crossing transfer necessarily reveals the net amount crossing between the pools. Timing and network metadata can create additional correlation opportunities.
THE CROWD HELPS MOST WHEN VALUE LIVES AND MOVES INSIDE THE CROWD.
OPTIONAL PRIVACY IS NOT THE SAME AS USELESS PRIVACY

Zcash has historically supported both transparent and shielded value. That means users and wallets can make choices that affect what becomes public. A transparent transaction does not inherit shielded privacy simply because it occurs on Zcash. A fully shielded transaction, however, uses the shielded protocol's cryptographic protections regardless of the existence of transparent addresses elsewhere in the system.
The meaningful question is therefore not simply whether privacy is optional. It is where the value is, how the transaction is constructed and what information crosses a visible boundary.
USAGE CHANGES THE ENVIRONMENT

When wallets keep funds shielded and shielded-to-shielded activity becomes ordinary, private transactions are less exceptional. When users repeatedly cross transparent boundaries in recognizable patterns, they can reveal information that the shielded protocol itself was designed not to publish.
THE DIFFERENCE IN ONE LINE.
CRYPTOGRAPHY HIDES THE LINK. THE CROWD MAKES THAT MISSING LINK MORE USEFUL.
